review_notes:
I read the whole file. I grepped Mathlib for other smooth-number or factored-number concepts. The only other users of `Nat.smoothNumbers`, `Nat.factoredNumbers` and `equivProdNat*` are in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/EulerProduct/Basic.lean`, and they depend on this file. Every other "smooth" hit is about differentiability or algebraic geometry. I found no independent Mathlib definition of the same concept.

Within the file, `smoothNumbers n` and `factoredNumbers s` are two definitions of one pattern, and `smoothNumbers n` is the case `s = range n`. The docstring says so and `smoothNumbers_eq_factoredNumbers` proves it, so the pairing is deliberate. The smooth API is a thin set of named specialisations that reduce to the factored API. `pow_mul_mem_smoothNumbers` also covers non-prime `p`, which the factored version does not. `smoothNumbersUpTo` and `roughNumbersUpTo` are new Finset-valued definitions with their own cardinality bounds, and I found no Mathlib equivalent. `factoredNumbers` is definitionally close to "`m ≠ 0` and `m.primeFactors ⊆ s`", but the file keeps `primeFactorsList` as the primary form and proves the equivalence with `mem_factoredNumbers_iff_primeFactors_subset`. I judged this a chosen representation, not a competing duplicate. I found nothing that justifies consolidation, so I abstain.
